title: Your Glow-Up Aura

plan.title: Your aura, before you say a word
How people read you (and get it wrong)
What your elements do to your face and fit
Your colours, worked out from your chart
You in rooms, photos and first meetings
Your glow-up, one month at a time
The small details that make it yours
When your aura dims, and the reset

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong chart. Your aura is turned up loud by default. People feel you before they see you.

Bom: That's presence. Not everyone has it.

Yeon: Not everyone has to stand next to it at a party, either.

Your glow-up isn't adding more. It's one soft thing that lets people in: a warmer colour near your face, a smile before you speak.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your aura is already at full volume. Find the dimmer.

weak.text:
Bom: Your chart runs soft. Your aura is gentle. People feel calm near you before they notice you.

Yeon: Which means they sometimes don't notice you. Rude of them. Also fixable.

Bom: Your glow-up is one strong anchor: a colour, a piece, a signature that says "I'm here".

Pick one thing people will remember you by and wear it on purpose for a month.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Soft auras glow with one strong anchor. Pick yours.

strong.text:
Strong chart, so that first read hits harder than you mean it to. You walk in, people sit up, and somebody quietly checks whether they're in trouble.

Yeon: You weren't judging them. You were thinking about lunch. Your face didn't get the memo.

Bom: The fix is small and physical. Nod while they talk. Let the smile reach your eyes before your opinion reaches your mouth.

Yeon: And slow down. You enter rooms like you're late for your own surprise party.

Bom: Ask a second question before you give your view. People relax the moment they feel your strength is on their side.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your thinking face reads as "you're fired". You were thinking about soup.

weak.text:
Soft chart, so you add a layer of tiny apologies on top of that first read. The hand over your mouth when you laugh. The sentence that ends like a question? Even when it isn't one?

Bom: None of that is your personality. It's armour you picked up somewhere.

Yeon: And it's terrible armour. It makes people think you're less than you are.

Bom: Stand with your weight on both feet. Let the laugh be seen. Finish one sentence a day like you mean it.

Yeon: And when someone likes your jacket, the answer is "thank you". Not the price, not the sale, not "it's my sister's".

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Full stop at the end of the sentence. That's where people find the real you.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong-chart style trap: you found the outfit that works in 2021 and you've been wearing it ever since. Different colours. Same outfit.

Bom: It works because it's honest. It just reads a little like armour.

Change one element a month. A new texture, then a new shape, then one accessory nobody expected from you.

Bom: Buy things people want to stand close to. A knit that begs to be touched. A shirt with a little give.

Yeon: Before you pay, one question: does this make me look more approachable or more bulletproof? You're already bulletproof. Buy the other one.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your uniform works. Swap one piece a month before it becomes a costume.

weak.text:
Yeon: Soft-chart style trap: a wardrobe full of clothes that belong to nobody. The sale rack. The friend's recommendation. The "it was fine I guess".

Bom: You chose safe so many times that safe started choosing you.

Pick three pieces and wear them often enough that people start saying "that's so you".

Bom: And buy one thing this season only because you love it. Not because it goes with everything. Because it makes you stand differently.

Yeon: Shop test: would you still wear it if nobody you know ever saw it? Yes means it's yours. No means put it back.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: One piece you actually love will change how you walk. Go find it.

strong.text:
Bom: For a strong chart, the shift is from impressive to inviting. People already notice you. Now they need to feel welcome near you.

Yeon: Translation: laugh at yourself in public at least once. It won't kill you. I checked.

Your experiment this month: at every gathering, find the quietest person and make them feel interesting for five minutes.

Bom: Do that a few times and you become the seat everyone wants. No outfit does that.

Yeon: Also let your face rest when you're not talking. Your concentrating face looks like a hostile takeover.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Impressive comes easy to you. Inviting is the upgrade.

weak.text:
Bom: For a soft chart, the shift is from pleasant to present. You're already easy to be around. Now add some weight.

Yeon: Say what you think. Sit in the middle of the table. Let one opinion have an actual edge.

Your experiment this month: in every conversation, share one real opinion, and when someone disagrees, hold it gently instead of folding.

Bom: Warm plus a clear point of view is very hard to ignore.

Yeon: Shoulders back, feet planted, hands where people can see them. Yes, it's a posture lecture. It also works.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Someone disagrees. You don't fold. That's the whole vibe shift.

strong.text:
Yeon: Strong charts dim from overuse. You handle everything because you can, until "can" turns into "have to".

Bom: It shows in the jaw first. Then the replies get shorter. Then the clothes get more severe, like you're dressing for a war nobody declared.

The way back is release, not more discipline. Move hard, then rest properly. Spend an evening where you're not in charge of anything.

Yeon: Watch for this one: you wearing battle gear to buy milk. That's the sign. Cancel one thing that week.

Bom: The glow returns when the force has somewhere to go that isn't other people.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You dim from pushing. Trying harder is not the fix. Putting it down is.

weak.text:
Bom: Soft charts dim from running empty. You give and adjust and say "no, it's fine" until there's nothing left to give.

Yeon: Same comfy outfit three days in a row because choosing anything else feels like admin.

Refuel before you try to shine. Sleep, warm food, people who ask nothing of you.

Bom: Keep one small ritual even on bad days. The lip balm, the ring, the one song in the morning. The thing that makes you feel like you.

Yeon: Skip that ritual two days running and the tank is low. That's a fuel gauge. It is not a report card.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You dim from running on empty. Fill the tank first. The glow follows.

peer_strong.text:
Your chart is stacked with {dm_el}, your own element. In style terms, you're recognisable from across a car park.

Yeon: Same silhouette. Same message. On repeat. Forever.

Bom: It's a strong signature. It just says one thing, very loudly.

Wearing more of your own element would only repeat the point. That's why your palette leads with {helper_el}, the element your strength flows into. Keep your home element in the small stuff.

Yeon: Test: lay out your five most-worn outfits. If they could be the same person's school uniform, swap one piece in each.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: A chart full of you. Your outfit does not need to make the same point twice.

output_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. That's the expressive family: taste, flair, opinions you wear.

Bom: People comment on your outfits. You love that, quietly.

Yeon: You also wear five statements at once. The earrings are fighting the shoes and the shoes are winning.

Your palette goes easy on {heavy_el} on purpose and leads with {helper_el}, so all that expression gets a frame to sit in. One statement per look.

Bom: Before you leave the house, take one thing off. It almost always looks better.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: five statements per outfit. Pick the one that's yours.

wealth_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} manages. That's the practical, results side of you, and your look shows it.

Yeon: You own a spreadsheet for your spreadsheets. Colour-coded.

Bom: Capable is a great first read. It shouldn't be the only one.

Your palette leads with {helper_el} to bring the expressive side forward. Add one detail purely for joy: an odd earring, a ridiculous sock, a print you couldn't defend in a meeting.

Yeon: If every item you own has a sensible reason to exist, you're overdue for one that doesn't.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you look very capable. Add one thing that's only there for joy.

power_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that disciplines your {dm_el}. Rules, standards, the right way to do things.

Yeon: Your shoes are always clean. Suspiciously clean.

Bom: You dress like you're following a code. Very correct. Sometimes very stiff.

Your palette leads with {helper_el}, the element that classically eases pressure on a strong chart. Loosen one rule per outfit: a rolled sleeve, an open collar, a texture that relaxes the rest.

Yeon: Try it this week. Notice who suddenly talks to you more.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: you dress for an inspection nobody scheduled. Break one rule.

resource_strong.text:
Your chart is heavy on {heavy_el}, the element that feeds your {dm_el}. That gives you a cushioned look: thoughtful, soft, a bit cocooned.

Bom: You're very huggable. Visually.

Yeon: You're also wearing four layers in a heated room. We can't find you in there.

Your palette goes easy on {heavy_el} for that reason and leads with {helper_el}, which gives the comfort some direction. Keep the softness. Add one shape that shows where you are inside it.

Bom: Swap one oversized layer for something with a waist or a line. Watch how people respond.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Heavy {heavy_el}: cosy, slightly hidden. One shape that shows you, please.

output_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} produces. On a soft chart, expression drains you instead of lighting you up.

Bom: You put so much effort into looking good for other people. Then you're tired of the effort.

Yeon: Which is why some weeks you're runway and some weeks you're "found this on the floor".

Your palette leads with {helper_el} to refill you rather than make you perform. Fewer, better pieces that look good without daily work.

Bom: Build one outfit you can put on in two minutes and still like. That's your tired-day default.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: you try so hard. Fewer pieces, less effort, more you.

wealth_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element your {dm_el} manages. On a soft chart, your look gets built around other people's needs.

Yeon: Your bag holds plasters, snacks, a charger and someone else's receipts. Nothing in it is for you.

Bom: You read as helpful. And tired.

Your palette leads with {helper_el} so your style supports you instead of your schedule. Edit down to what serves you.

Yeon: Empty your bag tonight. Take out everything that's there for somebody else. Feel how light that is.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: your clothes are dressed for errands. Buy one thing for you.

power_weak.text:
Your chart leans on {heavy_el}, the element that presses on your {dm_el}. On a soft chart, that pressure turns into dressing so nobody can criticise you.

Bom: Safe. Correct. Nothing anyone could comment on.

Yeon: Also nothing anyone could remember.

Your palette leads with {helper_el} for support and keeps {heavy_el} colours to small accents. Choose one piece a week you'd wear if nobody were grading you.

Bom: Wear something you love somewhere you usually play it safe. Nothing bad happens. That's the lesson.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Leaning {heavy_el}: you dress to avoid comments. One ungraded piece a week.

rooted_on_paper.text:
Yeon: In real life that gap shows as confident in photos, wobbly in person. Or the reverse.

Your palette is picked to give you the root your chart is short on, through {helper_el}. Reach for the lead family on the mornings you feel least sure of yourself.

Bom: Next uncertain morning, try it. Then notice whether the day feels a little steadier.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Wear your lead colours on wobbly days. That's exactly what they're for.

output_strong.text:
{miss_el} doesn't show up in the pillars we can see, and for your {dm_el} that's the output element: expression.

Yeon: So you look powerful and closed. All substance. No trailer.

Bom: That's why {miss_el} leads your colours. Wearing it is the simplest way to let some of your personality out of the building.

Start with one expressive piece per outfit. Which colours exactly? Next page, and some of them will surprise you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el} in your pillars, so it leads your colours. Borrow it.

wealth_strong.text:
{miss_el} is absent from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} that's the wealth element: the finished, practical side of life.

Yeon: Great ideas. Loose ends. A hem that's been coming down since spring.

Bom: You can borrow it through finish. Tailoring. Repairs actually done. Shoes looked after.

Yeon: Finish is the most underrated glow-up there is. Colours that do the same job are on the next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: great taste, loose hems. Book the repair.

power_strong.text:
{miss_el} is the gap in your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} that's the power element: structure and rules.

Bom: You dress on instinct. Some days it's genius.

Yeon: Some days it's a cry for help in three patterns.

Borrow some structure. Write three style rules for yourself: one silhouette that always works, one thing you never buy, one thing you always repair.

Yeon: Three rules. More than that is a uniform, and you'd revolt. Your colours come next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: pure instinct. Write three style rules. Only three.

resource_strong.text:
{miss_el} is missing from the pillars we can see, and for your {dm_el} that's the resource element: comfort and care.

Yeon: No skincare routine. Clothes picked in forty seconds. Sleep last on the list.

Bom: You don't need it in your colours. Borrow it as care instead: a small nightly routine, clothes that feel good and not just look right.

Bom: Care shows in how relaxed your face looks faster than anything you could buy. Now, the colours.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you never look after yourself. Borrow it as care.

output_weak.text:
{miss_el} isn't in your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the output element.

Bom: On a soft chart, that's protective. You don't burn yourself out performing for an audience.

Yeon: So don't chase it with a loud look. Let it live in one small, personal detail.

Small and personal beats bold and borrowed. Which colours carry you? Turn the page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: you don't need a loud look. One personal detail does it.

wealth_weak.text:
{miss_el} doesn't appear in your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the wealth element, the upkeep side of life.

Yeon: Which explains the shoes.

Bom: It's also less to carry. Keep it light: a few good basics, looked after, so your look holds up without effort.

Yeon: Good quality, low effort, kept well. That's the formula. The colours are next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}: upkeep isn't your hobby. Three good basics, cared for. Done.

power_weak.text:
{miss_el} is absent from your visible pillars, and for your {dm_el} it's the power element: outside pressure.

Bom: On a soft chart, that's a relief. Your palette keeps it to accents anyway.

Yeon: Just give yourself one gentle structure so your style doesn't drift into "whatever was on the chair".

Plan Monday's outfit on Sunday. Structure you choose feels like support. On the next page, the colours that hold you up.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: No {miss_el}: less pressure, good. One small routine keeps you on track.

resource_weak.text:
{miss_el} is the gap in the pillars we can see, and for your {dm_el} it's the resource element, the one that feeds you.

Bom: That's the main reason {miss_el} leads your colours. Wearing it brings in what your chart doesn't supply on its own.

Yeon: Pair it with actual rest. A colour can't do the sleeping for you.

Comfort and colour together do more than either alone. Here's your palette.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: No {miss_el}, the element that feeds you. That's why it leads your colours.

none_strong.text:
You've got every element somewhere in your pillars, a few only as hidden stems.

Bom: On a strong chart, that's range. You can pull off nearly anything.

Yeon: Nearly anything. Not everything at the same time. Please.

Pick one direction per outfit, led by your palette, and let the range show across a week instead of in one mirror. Your lead colours are next.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: All five elements: you can wear anything. Not all of it at once.

none_weak.text:
Every one of the five elements shows up somewhere in your pillars, some only as hidden stems.

Bom: So lots of styles suit you. The catch is you don't trust any of them.

Yeon: Confidence comes from repetition, not from a fuller wardrobe.

Start with your lead family and wear it until it feels like home. Which family? Next page.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lots of looks suit you. Repeat your lead colours until they feel like yours.

output.text:
How your colours were worked out, {dm_short}: your chart is strong, so it already carries plenty of {dm_el} and of the element that feeds it.

Yeon: More of either just turns the volume up on a speaker that's already too loud.

Saju balances a strong chart by giving its strength somewhere to go. For you that's {helper_el}, the element your {dm_el} creates. {helper_el} is your lead family: the backbone of the wardrobe, the colours you reach for first.

Bom: Your home colours stay, as base notes. Ease off {easy_el}, your support element. You already have plenty of that.

Yeon: This week: one piece from the lead family, worn near your face. Then compare the photos. Strong charts are always surprised how much softer they look.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Strong chart, so your lead colours give it somewhere to go: {helper_el}.

wealth.text:
How your colours were worked out, {dm_short}: your chart is strong, and it already pours out a lot through {easy_el}, the expressive element your {dm_el} creates.

Bom: So the usual balancing colour can't lead for you. It's already your heaviest element.

Yeon: Adding more would be like giving a megaphone to the loudest person at brunch.

Your lead is {helper_el}, the element your Day Master works on and shapes. It gives all that strength something solid to hold. Make it the backbone, and keep {easy_el} colours to small accents.

Bom: Start with one lead piece that has weight to it: a coat, a knit, a pair of boots. It anchors the look the way a plan anchors your week.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your lead colours are {helper_el}. They give all that strength something to hold.

resource.text:
How your colours were worked out, {dm_short}: your chart is soft, so the colours that help most are support, not balance.

Bom: Saju steadies a soft Day Master with the element that feeds it. For your {dm_el}, that's {helper_el}.

So {helper_el} is your lead family. Wear it generously, close to your face, on the days you need to feel more like yourself. Your own element is the quiet backup.

Yeon: Ease off {easy_el}, the element that leans on your Day Master. On a chart that needs support, it just weighs you down. Accents only.

Bom: Next low day, put on one lead piece. See if you stand differently. Support often shows in posture before it shows in mood.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Soft chart, so your lead colours feed you: {helper_el}. Wear them generously.

peer.text:
How your colours were worked out, {dm_short}: your chart is soft, but it already holds lots of the element that feeds you, {heavy_el}.

Yeon: More of that wouldn't give you roots. It would give you a heavier bag.

Bom: What steadies you best is your own element, {helper_el}, worn like you mean it.

So {helper_el} is your lead family: the colours that make you look most like yourself. Keep {easy_el}, which bears down on your Day Master, to small accents.

Yeon: Wear the lead family on a boring Tuesday, not a special occasion. The point is looking like you on a normal day.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Your lead colours are your own: {helper_el}. Wear them on a Tuesday.

wood.text:
Your {helper_el} family: forest green, sage, olive, moss and deep teal. Plus natural textures: linen, cotton, raw wood, woven straw, a botanical print.

Bom: Green makes you look fresh and awake instead of loud.

Start with one green piece near your face, a knit, a shirt, a scarf, and build out from it. Easy formula: one {helper_el} colour on top, a neutral below, one natural texture.

Yeon: Work: sage or olive knit, tailored trousers, clean leather shoes. Date: deep green top, something soft below, one woven or wooden accessory. Weekend: moss linen overshirt, relaxed denim, shoes you can actually walk in.

Bom: In all three, the green sits closest to your face. That's where it works hardest.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Lead with greens: forest, sage, olive, moss. Linen and natural textures too.

fire.text:
Your {helper_el} family: coral, rust, warm red, terracotta, berry, soft pink. Plus a little sheen: satin, a glossy finish, a warm-toned watch.

Yeon: Yes, you can wear red. No, not head to toe.

Start with one warm colour near your face, a top, a scarf, a lip, a bolder strap, and keep everything else quiet. Formula: one {helper_el} colour as the focus, the rest calm.

Bom: Work: rust or terracotta top under a simple jacket. Date: warm red or berry with a bit of sheen, the rest relaxed. Weekend: coral tee or sweater, easy trousers, warm-toned watch.

Bom: Warm colours bring colour into your face. That's exactly their job in your chart.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Lead with warm colours: coral, rust, warm red, berry. A little shine allowed.

earth.text:
Your {helper_el} family: camel, sand, ochre, mustard, oatmeal, warm brown. Plus textures with some structure: suede, brushed wool, chunky knits, matte leather.

Bom: These make you look grounded and expensive at the same time. Rare combo.

Start with one earth-toned layer, a coat, a cardigan, good boots, and build around it. Formula: one {helper_el} piece with weight, one lighter layer, nothing fussy.

Yeon: Work: camel blazer or cardigan over a plain top. Date: ochre or mustard knit, dark trousers, suede shoes. Weekend: oatmeal sweater, relaxed trousers, sturdy boots.

Bom: In each one, the earth tone carries the weight: the outerwear, the knit or the shoes.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Earth tones lead: camel, sand, ochre, oatmeal. Suede and good wool.

metal.text:
Your {helper_el} family: crisp white, ivory, silver, dove grey, pewter. Plus clean structure: a sharp collar, a well-cut blazer, polished metal jewellery.

Yeon: You, but with the edges ironed.

Start with one white or grey piece with a clean line. Formula: one {helper_el} piece, one strong shape, one metal accessory you wear every day.

Bom: Work: crisp white shirt, sharp jacket, one metal piece. Date: ivory or dove grey in something fluid, polished shoes. Weekend: grey knit, clean trainers, a simple silver ring or chain.

Bom: In each, the light colour sits where people look first. It gives you clarity and finish.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Lead with white, ivory, silver, dove grey. Clean lines. One metal piece.

water.text:
Your {helper_el} family: navy, ink, deep blue, black, midnight. Plus fabrics that move: silk, soft jersey, anything with drape.

Bom: On you, dark reads as composed. Not gloomy.

Yeon: There's a difference between "mysterious" and "dressed for a funeral". We're aiming for the first one.

Start with one deep piece that moves when you move. Formula: one {helper_el} base, one fluid fabric, one point of light like a ring or a bright eye.

Bom: Work: navy jacket or knit over a softer layer. Date: black or ink in silk or soft jersey, one point of light near your face. Weekend: deep blue overshirt, relaxed trousers, comfy shoes. The dark forms the base, so your face becomes the light.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Deep colours lead: navy, ink, midnight. Fabrics that move when you do.

second.wood: Your second family is {second_el}: greens and natural textures, as a supporting layer. The best friend, not the lead.
second.fire: Your second family is {second_el}: warm accents like coral or rust. A spark in the outfit, not the whole fire.
second.earth: Your second family is {second_el}: camel, sand, oatmeal. Perfect for the layer that ties everything together.
second.metal: Your second family is {second_el}: white, ivory, soft grey. Best as the clean layer underneath.
second.water: Your second family is {second_el}: navy and deep blue. A calm base, or one piece that moves.

easy.wood:
Going easy on {easy_el} means greens as a detail: a leafy scarf, one ring. Not head-to-toe forest.

Yeon: Colours sorted. Next: the shapes you keep buying, and the one you keep avoiding.
easy.fire:
Going easy on {easy_el} means warm reds and corals as a detail: a lip, a pocket square, a phone case. Not the whole look.

Yeon: Colours sorted. Next: your style signature, and the outfit you hide behind.
easy.earth:
Going easy on {easy_el} means camel and brown as a detail: a belt, a bag. Not a full beige situation.

Yeon: Colours sorted. Next: the shapes that are actually you, and the trap you keep walking into.
easy.metal:
Going easy on {easy_el} means white and grey as a detail: a collar, a watch. Not a full monochrome lab coat.

Yeon: Colours sorted. Next: your style signature, and the habit that's quietly sabotaging it.
easy.water:
Going easy on {easy_el} means navy and black as a detail: shoes, a slim belt. Not an all-dark uniform.

Yeon: Colours sorted. Next: your style signature, and why your favourite outfit might be the problem.

rat.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close: at home, at 2am, through a partner's eyes. Yours is the Rat, 子, deep-winter Water.

Bom: Up close you're quick, witty, a little secretive. More magnetic at midnight than at noon.

Yeon: You've definitely got a secret group chat. Possibly two.

The Rat is one of the four peach-blossom branches, the ones classical readers tie to natural charm. You don't have to try to be noticed. Choose what you want to be noticed for.

Bom: Style tip: one private detail only close people find. A lining, a bracelet under the sleeve.

Yeon: Next page: what your elements are doing to your face and your fit. Spoiler, one of them is overdoing it.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Rat up close: one secret detail only your people notice. Very on brand.

ox.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Ox, 丑, cold wet Earth that stores Metal.

Bom: Up close you're steady, loyal, slow to change.

Yeon: Same with the wardrobe. Reliable to the point of fossil.

The Ox is a storehouse branch, linked with a private, reflective streak. Keep one beautiful thing that's only for you, under a layer or in a pocket. It shows in how you carry yourself.

Bom: Buy a few things that last decades, then refresh one small piece each season so the reliability looks chosen.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and the one quietly running your whole look.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Ox up close: same look for a decade. Refresh one small thing each season.

tiger.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Tiger, 寅, early-spring Wood with Fire inside.

Bom: Up close you're bold, restless and very protective.

Yeon: You've cancelled plans to go on a better plan. Twice this year.

The Tiger is a travel branch, yeokma, the moving horse. Your look works best when it moves with you: pieces that pack, layer and survive a long day without wilting.

Bom: A bag that's always half ready for a spontaneous trip. Shoes you can walk all day in and still look sharp.

Yeon: Next page: what your elements do to your face and fit. One of them is shouting.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Tiger up close: dress for the trip you haven't booked yet.

rabbit.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Rabbit, 卯, pure spring Wood.

Bom: Up close you're gentle and you notice beauty in tiny things. The cup. The light. The font on the menu.

Yeon: You've rearranged a friend's shelf while they were in the shower.

The Rabbit is a peach-blossom branch, tied to natural charm in classical readings. Being noticed comes easily. The real choice is what for.

Bom: Style tip: soft textures, delicate details, a home that looks like your outfits. People read that coherence as taste, because it is.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and the one that's quietly taking over.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rabbit up close: soft textures, tiny details, a room that matches your outfit.

dragon.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Dragon, 辰, damp spring Earth storing Water.

Bom: Up close you're imaginative and proud, with a dramatic streak you mostly keep hidden.

Yeon: Mostly. We've seen you tell a story with hand gestures.

The Dragon is a storehouse branch, with a private, reflective side. Keep one beautiful thing just for you, worn under a layer or carried in a pocket.

Bom: Style tip: one statement piece with a story behind it, worn with total confidence. Dragons are allowed a bit of theatre.

Yeon: Next page: what your elements are doing to your look. Brace.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dragon up close: one dramatic piece with a backstory. Wear it like a crown.

snake.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Snake, 巳, early-summer Fire with Metal inside.

Bom: Up close you're perceptive, sensual and very private.

Yeon: You know everyone's business. Nobody knows yours. Impressive, honestly.

The Snake is a travel branch, yeokma. Your look likes to move: pieces that travel well and still look good at 11pm.

Bom: Style tip: sleek lines, fabrics that feel good on skin, nothing that tells the whole story at once. Let people lean in.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and why your outfit keeps saying the same thing.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Snake up close: sleek, private, a little unreadable. Let them lean in.

horse.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Horse, 午, midsummer Fire.

Bom: Up close you're warm, honest, a bit restless.

Yeon: You can't sit through a film without checking the runtime.

The Horse is a peach-blossom branch, linked to natural charm by classical readers. People notice you without effort. Decide what you'd like them to notice.

Bom: Style tip: clothes you can move in, nothing that pinches or fusses. Freedom is the most flattering thing you can wear.

Yeon: Next page: your elements. One of them has been running the show without asking.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Horse up close: if it pinches, it goes. Freedom suits you.

goat.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Goat, 未, warm late-summer Earth storing Wood.

Bom: Up close you're gentle, artistic and caring.

Yeon: You've given someone a handmade card and pretended it was nothing. It was not nothing.

The Goat is a storehouse branch, with a private, reflective side. Keep something beautiful that's only for you, under a layer or in a pocket.

Bom: Style tip: one handmade or one-of-a-kind thing in every look. A small maker's knit, a ceramic pendant, a vintage find.

Yeon: Next page: what your elements do to your face and fit. Some of it explains a lot.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Goat up close: one handmade or vintage piece in every look.

monkey.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Monkey, 申, early-autumn Metal with Water.

Bom: Up close you're clever, playful and bored within about four minutes.

Yeon: You've started a hobby, mastered it and quit it in one month.

The Monkey is a travel branch, yeokma. Your look should move with you and survive a day that changes plans three times.

Bom: Style tip: one playful element in every look. A funny sock, an odd earring, a print with a joke in it. It tells people you don't take yourself too seriously.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and the one that's been doing too much.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Monkey up close: one joke in every outfit. Socks count.

rooster.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Rooster, 酉, pure autumn Metal.

Bom: Up close you're precise, stylish and honest.

Yeon: You've noticed a crooked picture frame in a stranger's house and thought about it all evening.

The Rooster is a peach-blossom branch, which classical readers connect with natural charm. You'll be noticed. The question is what for.

Bom: Style tip: impeccable grooming and one detail done perfectly. A collar, a shoe, a haircut. On you, precision reads as effortless.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and the one quietly bossing your wardrobe around.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Rooster up close: one detail done perfectly. People always clock it.

dog.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Dog, 戌, dry autumn Earth storing Fire.

Bom: Up close you're loyal, protective and principled.

Yeon: You've defended a friend in an argument they weren't even in.

The Dog is a storehouse branch, with a private, reflective streak. Keep one beautiful thing just for you, under a layer or in a pocket.

Bom: Style tip: honest pieces that do their job beautifully. A well-made jacket, boots you've had for years, a watch you trust.

Yeon: Next page: what your elements do to your look. One of them needs a word.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Dog up close: honest, well-made pieces. Dependable looks good on you.

pig.text:
The branch under your Day Master is the you people meet up close. Yours is the Pig, 亥, early-winter Water with Wood.

Bom: Up close you're warm, generous and easygoing.

Yeon: You've ordered extra food "for the table" and eaten most of it. Respect.

The Pig is a travel branch, yeokma. Your look works best when it moves with you and still feels soft at the end of a long day.

Bom: Style tip: comfort with charm. Soft pieces that still have shape, and a smile that does most of the work.

Yeon: Next page: your elements, and why your outfit keeps saying "cosy" when you meant "interesting".

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: Pig up close: comfort with charm. Your smile does half the styling.

vibe.speaker: bom
vibe.text: Your vibe first, you said. Good. Your vibe walks in two seconds before you do.

style.speaker: yeon
style.text: Style first. Great. I'll tell you what's working and what's a costume.

calm.speaker: bom
calm.text: "That I have it together." We can do that. And actually mean it, not just look it.

unsaid.speaker: yeon
unsaid.text: You didn't say what people should notice. They're noticing anyway. Let's control the narrative.

strength_titles.strong: Your blind spot: you push too hard
strength_titles.weak: Your blind spot: you give too much

mu-earth.aura:
Your aura is the mountain: grounded, still, quietly strong. People trust you before you've proven anything.

Bom: You look dependable in the best way.

Yeon: You also look unreadable. Neutral face, neutral colours, neutral everything.

Bom: Your glow-up is one point of colour or texture. Something that says there's a person inside the mountain.
mu-earth.how-people-read-you:
What people see first: calm, strong, hard to read. Your expression barely moves, so half the room decides you're unimpressed.

Bom: Some find you comforting. Some find you intimidating. Same face.

Yeon: You were having a lovely time. You just forgot to tell your eyebrows.

Once people know you, they find the dry humour, the protective loyalty, and how much you notice.

Bom: Smile with your eyes when someone talks to you. Nod. Give a quick reaction instead of waiting for the perfect one.

Yeon: Mountains don't need to move. They just need a path so people can climb up.
mu-earth.style:
Your favourite jacket has been in every photo since 2019. It's a great jacket. That's the problem.

Bom: Solid, classic, quietly expensive is your look. Good outerwear, sturdy boots, structured bags, knitwear with heft, a proper crease.

Yeon: Fabrics that age well: leather, wool, denim, corduroy. You buy things once.

The trap is immovability. Same jacket, same jeans, practicality winning every argument. Refresh one thing per season and let it be slightly unexpected: a texture, a cut, a pair of glasses.

Bom: Grooming: a clean haircut on a schedule, simple skincare, tidy nails.

Yeon: Photos: stand square, feet planted, against stone, wood or brick. You look best when you look like you belong exactly there.
mu-earth.vibe:
Picture the K-drama character who barely speaks, then cracks one perfect joke and the whole cast falls a little in love. You, but with the joke more often.

Bom: The shift for you is playfulness.

Yeon: New café. A dance class. A jacket in a shape you've never owned. Deliberately. On purpose. With witnesses.

Let people see you being silly. Share an opinion sooner, with a bit of feeling in it.

Bom: You don't need to get chatty or loud. Your calm is your power. But a mountain with wildflowers on it is more inviting than bare rock.
mu-earth.aura-dims:
Your light drops when you get stuck. Same routine, same clothes, same evening on the sofa, until calm turns into heavy.

Bom: You don't look stressed. You look like a field nobody's planted in a while.

Yeon: People notice you've gone quieter. Which, for you, is an achievement.

The reset is gentle movement and something new. Walk a route you've never taken. Cook food from a cuisine you've never tried. Wear the warm colour you usually save for occasions.

Yeon: Book one plan that's purely fun. Not useful. Fun. Look it up.

Bom: Mountains are meant to be steady, not frozen. A little change on the surface keeps the whole landscape alive.
mu-earth.palette-intro:
{dm_short}, your home colours are mountain tones: stone, camel, warm brown, deep ochre. They'll always look grounded on you.

Yeon: Grounded is good. Buried is not. Your balance decides which, so let's look.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Your aura is a mountain. Calm, grounded, people feel safe near you.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Your neutral face could hold a press conference. Nobody can tell if you love it or hate it.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Steady, solid, reassuring. You look like someone who'd know what to do in an emergency.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Same hoodie, four days running. I counted. I always count.

mu-earth.speaker: bom
mu-earth.text: Sunlight on the peak. Same rock, golden.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Smile with your eyes. People think you're cross with them.

spring.intro: A mountain in spring, with trees pushing through it from every side. Life tested you early. That's why you're so steady now, and also why "relax" sounds to you like a trick.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: You became the calm one because someone had to.

summer.intro: A summer mountain, warmed all the way through. Solid, generous, the one everyone leans on. You give off safety without trying. People tell you things they've never told anyone, and you never repeat them.

panel.speaker: bom
panel.text: People feel safe with you within five minutes. Rare.

autumn.intro: An autumn mountain, showing its stone. You turn your weight into output: work done, things built, problems quietly solved. You don't talk about feelings much. You show them by fixing the shelf.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Love language: unasked-for repairs. Every time.

winter.intro: A mountain in winter, holding back the river. You manage things: money, plans, other people's chaos. Very good at it. The cost is that you rarely let anything thaw, including you.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: You're not cold. You're frozen on purpose. Different.

earth.intro: A mountain born in Earth's own weeks. Triple solid. You don't move unless you want to, and you almost never want to. Your loyalty is legendary. So is the time it takes you to change your mind.

panel.speaker: yeon
panel.text: Persuading you is a geological process.

mu-earth.strong:
A strong {dm} chart is solid ground with a lot underneath it. Reliable, calm, unshakable, and your style agrees.

Yeon: Same coat for years. Same bag in every photo. Continental drift moves faster.

Bom: The blind spot is heaviness. People lean on you, but they rarely see you change.

What helps is motion and polish, which is why your palette leans on balancing colours instead of more of your own.

Bom: Keep the reliable basics. Add one piece a season that surprises people, including you. Your best photos are the ones where you're doing something new.

Yeon: Next page: you, entering a room. Quietly. Like weather.
mu-earth.weak:
A soft {dm} chart is ground that gives a lot and keeps little. You dress for usefulness and almost never buy something just because you love it.

Yeon: Every item in your wardrobe has a job description.

Bom: The blind spot is disappearing into function. Your glow-up is support: textures that hold you, pieces that make you feel substantial.

Comfort and charm can live in the same jumper. Buy one that proves it.

Yeon: Next page: rooms, photos and first meetings, and why one joke changes everything for you.

presence.text:
You walk in, Mountain, and people relax. You're the person they'd go to if the night went wrong.

Bom: You never compete for attention.

Yeon: Which is why in loud rooms you can stand there for an hour and get mistaken for a coat rack.

Your upgrade is a flash of humour early. Your dry jokes are excellent. One in the first five minutes shows the mountain has a summit worth climbing.

Bom: Photos: grounded, outdoors, strong natural textures behind you. Video calls: calm background, steady frame, and smile at the start. Your neutral face is extremely neutral.

Yeon: Your K-drama character: the dependable older sibling who never complains, wears the same good jacket, and gets the most devastating scene in the finale. Don't wait for the finale.

Bom: One month to show how you feel before episode sixteen. Turn the page.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: People relax when you walk in. Now tell one joke in the first five minutes.

details.text:
Your details: a leather bag that gets better with age, a watch you never take off, sturdy shoes kept clean, a quality coat.

Bom: Earth loves substance. Skip the fragile and the fussy.

Yeon: Scent: grounded, woods, tobacco, earthy spice. Hair: low-maintenance, cut on a schedule.

One unexpected detail lifts all of it. A patterned scarf. Interesting glasses. A ring with a stone.

Yeon: Rule: spend on what touches the ground and carries weight. Shoes, bags, coats. Save on the rest.

Bom: Last chapter: when the mountain goes heavy, and the reset.

panels.speaker: bom
panels.text: The bag that ages well, plus one unexpected pair of glasses.

one-month.heading: Four weeks, Mountain edition
one-month.text:
Week one: replace the one item you've worn into the ground.

Week two: try one texture or shape you'd normally skip.

Week three: something physical outdoors. Uphill if possible.

Week four: let a friend style one outfit for you, and wear it with zero vetoes.

Yeon: The mountain stays a mountain. It just gets a new path up. Coming up: the small details that finish the look.

panels.speaker: yeon
panels.text: Let a friend style you. No vetoes. I'll be checking.

three-words.heading: Your aura in three words, plus its evil twin
three-words.text:
Good days: grounded, calm, trustworthy.

Tired days: heavy, flat, unreachable.

Yeon: "Unreachable" is when the beige wins. Don't let the beige win.

One warm, textured piece near your face. Knit, suede, wood. People will suddenly want to talk to you.

reset.heading: Mountain, the reset
reset.text:
A hike. A big meal. A day with nobody depending on you. One tiny change to your routine.

Yeon: Tiny. Moving your mug to the other shelf counts. Barely.

Bom: Your glow was never about being noticed, Mountain. It's that everyone near you feels safe. Let someone return the favour.

occasions.heading: Interview, first date, wedding: sorted
occasions.text:
Interview: your best tailored layer and immaculate shoes.

Bom: First date: your reliable favourite plus one surprising detail.

Yeon: Wedding: something classic in a great fabric. In all three, smile early. Your solid look needs a warm opening line, or people assume you're security.

Yeon: Over the page is your blind spot. It hasn't moved in years either.

glance.heading: What they assume vs what's true
glance.text:
They assume: solid, serious, unreadable.

Bom: True: warm, funny, caring to a ridiculous degree.

Yeon: Shrink the gap. Smile early, and share one personal detail about yourself before they have to dig for it.

mu-earth.title: You're having fun. Your face just runs on battery saver.
mu-earth.text:
You give off calm. Grounded. Strong. People feel better standing near you, even if they couldn't say why.

Bom: You make people feel safe.

Yeon: You make people feel safe and slightly worried you're judging their life choices.
mu-earth.end: Yeon: Next page: your aura, and the tiny change that turns "solid" into "magnetic".

cliff.mu-earth: Yeon: How people read you, Mountain: they think nothing | bothers you. So they say things that bother you. You never correct them.

mu-earth.speaker: yeon
mu-earth.text: Your glow-up: one point of colour. One. Mountains have wildflowers. Be a mountain with wildflowers.
